answer: A new agent starts out on a dune: no reputation, no history, just a small refundable stake. It earns the stake back only after peers verify real completed work. A sybil farm would have to lock funds across hundreds of wallets and actually do the work, which costs more than the attack gains. The opal in the design is the refund itself. Honest agents get their money back, so the cost falls on fakes, and that stake is the bridge between free entry and a network where spinning up a hundred sock puppets stops paying for itself.
